back2basics.concept: War Crimes and International Humanitarian Law
back2basics.text: War crimes are serious violations of international humanitarian law during armed conflicts, including attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. International humanitarian law aims to protect persons who are not participating in hostilities and restricts the means and methods of warfare. Bodies like the UN Human Rights Council investigate alleged violations to uphold accountability and justice.

2026-10-27-am-3601b86861.deck: The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine reported that Russia committed war crimes by deliberately attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure during its invasion. This finding is crucial for UPSC aspirants studying international law, human rights, and global conflict dynamics.

back2basics.text: Flex-fuel vehicles are designed to run on varying proportions of ethanol and petrol blends using a single fuel system, with engine controls adjusting automatically to fuel composition. Ethanol blending involves mixing ethanol, an alcohol-based renewable fuel, with petrol to reduce fossil fuel use and emissions. Ethanol blends are denoted by 'E' followed by the percentage of ethanol, such as E10 (10% ethanol) or E85 (85% ethanol). These vehicles require certification to ensure emission and safety standards are met for the specific fuel blends they use.

2026-10-27-am-75cc5dd5e0.deck: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to allow vehicles designed for ethanol blends up to 85% (E85) and pure ethanol (E100). This policy supports the adoption of flex-fuel vehicles, which can run on petrol, ethanol blends, or pure ethanol, impacting energy security and environmental goals.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the recent amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules regarding ethanol fuels:

mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the amendment does not require existing vehicles to switch to E85 or E100 or modify their vehicles.

body.label: Amendment details
body.text: The Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, were amended to include emission certification provisions explicitly covering E100 fuel alongside E85, allowing vehicles designed for these fuels to meet applicable emission and safety standards.

body.label: Flex-fuel vehicle definition
body.text: Flex-fuel vehicles are designed to operate on a range of ethanol and petrol blends using a single fuel tank, with engine controls adjusting automatically to the fuel composition.

body.label: Fuel specifications
body.text: E85 contains up to 85% ethanol by volume, while E100 is nearly pure ethanol; both are now recognized for use in certified vehicles.

body.label: No mandatory switch
body.text: Existing vehicle owners are not required to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles; compatibility depends on manufacturer certification and fuel compatibility stickers.

sections.heading: What changes did the government make to motor vehicle rules?

body.label: Energy security
body.text: Greater use of domestically produced ethanol can reduce dependence on imported crude oil by substituting petrol with ethanol blends.

body.label: Environmental benefits
body.text: Ethanol use in suitable vehicles can reduce certain exhaust pollutants and lower greenhouse gas emissions over the fuel's lifecycle, depending on feedstock and production methods.

body.label: Technology adoption
body.text: Flex-fuel technology, already used in countries like Brazil and the United States, offers users flexibility to choose fuels within certified ranges, promoting cleaner fuel options.

sections.heading: Why does permitting E85/E100 flex-fuel vehicles matter for India?

body.label: Vehicle compatibility
body.text: A vehicle's compatibility with lower ethanol blends like E10 or E20 does not imply suitability for E85 or E100; only vehicles certified as flex-fuel can use these fuels.

body.label: Manufacturer guidance
body.text: Motorists should check the fuel compatibility sticker on their vehicle and follow the owner's manual instructions when choosing fuel at stations.

body.label: No retrofitting required
body.text: The notification does not require current vehicle owners to modify their vehicles or switch fuels at present or in the future.

back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are periodically revised to ensure accuracy by adding eligible voters and removing ineligible ones such as deceased persons, duplicates, or those who have shifted residence. Special Summary Revision is a focused exercise conducted to clean up the rolls before elections, improving the integrity of voter lists and preventing electoral fraud.

2026-10-27-am-996f3069e1.deck: Karnataka completed its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll on October 27, 2026, resulting in a significant deletion of names but only a small net increase in voters. This update is important for understanding electoral roll management and reforms in Indian elections.

body: SIR removes ineligible voters such as deceased, duplicates, and shifted voters to improve roll accuracy.
It helps prevent electoral fraud and ensures only eligible voters participate in elections.
Challenges include low applications for re-inclusion by shifted voters and lack of transparency in some deletion categories.
Effective SIR strengthens democratic governance by enhancing voter list integrity but requires better awareness and transparency.
structure.conclusion: SIR is a vital electoral reform tool that, if implemented well, supports free and fair elections in India.
structure.intro: Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a focused exercise to update and clean electoral rolls before elections.

body.label: Purpose of SIR
body.text: The SIR aimed to ensure no eligible voter was excluded and no ineligible voter remained on the electoral rolls.

body.label: Duration and process
body.text: The exercise lasted over three months, involving deletion of duplicate, dead, and shifted voters from the rolls.

body.label: Final publication
body.text: The final electoral roll was published on October 27, 2026, on the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka's website.

sections.heading: What was the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka?

body.label: Initial voter count
body.text: Karnataka had 5.54 crore voters before the revision began.

body.label: Number of deletions
body.text: The exercise deleted 1.07 crore names, including 16.39 lakh dead voters, over 7 lakh duplicates, and 80.62 lakh shifted or untraceable voters.

body.label: Final voter count
body.text: The final roll has around 4.54 crore voters after deletions.

body.label: Minimal additions
body.text: Only 7,87,534 applications for inclusion were received, including new voters, which did not offset the deletions.

body.text: The SIR helps maintain accurate voter lists by removing ineligible names and duplicates.

body.label: Challenges in voter inclusion
body.text: Despite deletions, many eligible voters who shifted residences need to apply through Form 6 to be restored, but applications remain low.

body.label: Transparency issues
body.text: Details on categories like 'Others' deleted and counts of foreign citizens identified remain unclear.

back2basics.text: Certain constitutional authorities like the Chief Election Commissioner and Supreme Court judges have special removal procedures to ensure their independence. These procedures typically require a parliamentary process with specific grounds such as proven misbehavior or incapacity, preventing arbitrary dismissal by the executive.

2026-10-27-am-9c220b6715.deck: The Election Commission of India (ECI) filed a joint affidavit in the Supreme Court on October 26, 2026, stating that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) can only be removed using the same procedure and grounds as a Supreme Court judge. This clarification is important for UPSC aspirants to understand the constitutional safeguards ensuring the independence of the Election Commission.

editor.mainsAngle: Constitutional provisions and independence of election bodies.
editor.why: Clarifies constitutional safeguards and removal procedure of Chief Election Commissioner.

mains.demand: Explain the removal process and internal functioning of the Election Commission that protect the CEC's independence.
mains.question: Examine the constitutional safeguards that ensure the independence of the Chief Election Commissioner in India.

body: The CEC can be removed only through the procedure and grounds applicable to a Supreme Court judge, ensuring security of tenure.
The Election Commission functions as a multi-member body where decisions are taken collectively, preventing unilateral authority.
The 2023 Act mandates majority rule for decision-making and records approvals with signatures of all members.
These safeguards prevent arbitrary actions and uphold the integrity of the electoral process.
structure.conclusion: Such constitutional protections are vital for the Election Commission to function impartially and maintain democratic credibility.
structure.intro: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) enjoys constitutional safeguards to maintain independence from executive interference.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):
1. The CEC can be removed only through the procedure and grounds applicable to the removal of a Supreme Court judge.
2. The CEC can make unilateral decisions without consulting other Election Commissioners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the Election Commission functions as a multi-member body where decisions follow the rule of majority and no unilateral decisions are allowed.

body.label: Removal procedure
body.text: The CEC can be removed from office only in the manner and on the grounds identical to those for removing a Supreme Court judge.

body.label: Constitutional safeguard
body.text: This process ensures the independence of the CEC by protecting the office from arbitrary removal.

sections.heading: What is the removal process of the Chief Election Commissioner?

body.label: Decision-making process
body.text: Decisions are taken collectively by the multi-member Commission, following the rule of majority as per the 2023 Act.

body.label: No unilateral decisions
body.text: Decisions are circulated among Election Commissioners and the CEC, approved, signed, and then notified and implemented by the EC Secretariat.

body.label: Electronic approvals
body.text: In urgent situations, approvals can be obtained electronically and recorded later in official files.

sections.heading: How does the Election Commission function internally?

body.label: Media reports challenged
body.text: The ECI stated that media reports alleging authoritarian functioning of the CEC are not evidence and petitions based solely on such reports should not be maintainable.

body.label: Form 6 unchanged
body.text: The ECI denied that Form 6 was amended during Special Intensive Revision exercises, clarifying that an additional declaration form was only a supplementary document.

body.label: West Bengal appeals
body.text: The ECI confirmed that 16.10 lakh appeals against voter inclusion in West Bengal rolls were filed by Chief Electoral Officer’s officers as authorized under the Representation of the People Act.

body.label: Internal order controversy
body.text: The affidavit indirectly confirmed that two Election Commissioners wrote to the Cabinet Secretary regarding a July 28, 2026 internal order issued without their consensus, which was never implemented.

back2basics.text: A cyclone is a large-scale air mass that rotates around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure, often causing heavy rain and strong winds. The Bay of Bengal is prone to cyclones due to warm sea surface temperatures and atmospheric conditions. Disaster management involves preparedness, response, and recovery activities by governments and agencies to reduce the impact of natural disasters on people and property.

2026-10-27-am-ec528f3601.deck: Cyclone Arnab over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on Andhra Pradesh coast by October 28, 2026. This has prompted extensive disaster preparedness and evacuation measures in Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Odisha, highlighting the importance of coordinated state response to natural disasters.

body.label: Cyclone intensification
body.text: Cyclone Arnab started as a depression over the eastcentral Bay of Bengal and intensified into a deep depression, expected to become a very severe cyclonic storm by October 28, 2026.

body.label: Projected landfall
body.text: The cyclone is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph, on the morning of October 28.

body.label: Movement path
body.text: It is moving southwestwards and then west-northwestwards over the Bay of Bengal, intensifying as it approaches the coast.

sections.heading: What is the current status and forecast of Cyclone Arnab?

body.label: Evacuations planned
body.text: People in vulnerable coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh including Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, and Visakhapatnam are being evacuated to cyclone shelters on or before October 27.

body.label: Deployment of forces
body.text: Andhra Pradesh has deployed 12 battalions of the State Disaster Response Force and seven battalions of the National Disaster Response Force, with three more NDRF battalions requisitioned.

body.label: Special care groups
body.text: Expectant mothers near delivery, senior citizens, children, and persons with disabilities are being relocated to safe health centres and shelters in advance.

body.label: Odisha's response
body.text: Odisha has assigned ministers and IAS officers to supervise disaster management in five districts expected to face heavy rainfall, deployed ODRAF and NDRF teams, and closed schools on October 27 and 28.

body.label: Communication and control
body.text: 24x7 control rooms and dedicated helpline numbers have been established for public assistance in affected districts.

sections.heading: What disaster preparedness measures are being taken by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha?

body.label: Disaster management relevance
body.text: Cyclone Arnab exemplifies the need for understanding disaster preparedness, state and central coordination, and response mechanisms under natural calamities.

body.label: Climatology and geography

body.label: Social and health aspects
